issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. The diff only adds a ring-based seed generator, `_ring_seed`, which uses the existing seeded rng. There is no file or network access and no pasted coordinates.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. All five partitions add up to 26, which matches _N, so the noise array shape (_N, 2) is consistent. Clipping to [0.05, 0.95] keeps the seeds inside the square. Valid output is still left to the existing optimiser and shrink step.
The candidate scored -2.6343 against the incumbent's -2.6360. Lower loss is better, so the candidate is worse by about 0.0017. That matches the provisional decision to reject.

Each side has only one run, so the variance can't be estimated from the data and I can't recompute z. The reported z = -1195.5 matches a 0.0017 gap divided by an assumed noise of about 1e-6 × √2, i.e. the stated run-to-run noise rather than a measured spread. Treat the size of z as an artifact of that assumption, but its sign and the decision are right.

This is not new in the diff, but it matters: the 200 s wall-clock cutoff in the incumbent loop makes the number of restarts depend on the clock. Results may not repeat exactly even with a fixed seed. Separately, alternating ring and uniform seeds halves the uniform restarts within the same time limit, which may explain the regression.
